title: Compute Optimal Tokenization
abstract: arXiv:2605.01188v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Scaling laws enable the optimal selection of data amount and language model size, yet the impact of the data unit, the token, on this relationship remains underexplored. In this work, we systematically investigate how the information granularity of tokens, controlled by the compression rate (i.e., average bytes of text per token), affects scaling trends. We train 988 latent tokenized models (BLT) ranging from 50M to 7B parameters that enable setting the desired compression rate. This flexibility allows us to study the role of compression rate well beyond 4.57 bytes per token obtained with a popular BPE tokenizer. Our experiments reveal that in compute-optimal configurations, model parameter counts scale proportionally to data size measured in bytes, not in tokens as commonly perceived (Kaplan et al., 2020; Hoffmann et al., 2022). Furthermore, we discover that the optimal compression rate differs from the one obtained with BPE and dec

translated_abstract: 缩放定律使我们能够最优地选择数据量和语言模型规模，然而作为数据基本单位的“词元”对这一关系的影响仍未得到充分探索。在这项工作中，我们系统地研究了词元的信息粒度——由压缩率（即每个词元平均对应的文本字节数）所控制——如何影响缩放趋势。我们训练了988个潜在词元化模型（BLT），参数量从5000万到70亿不等，这些模型允许设定所需的压缩率。这种灵活性使我们能够研究远超常用BPE分词器所得的每词元4.57字节的压缩率范围。我们的实验揭示，在计算最优配置下，模型参数量与以字节（而非通常认为的词元）衡量的数据规模成正比地缩放。此外，我们发现最优压缩率不同于BPE分词器所得的结果，并且随……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过训练988个不同压缩率的潜在词元化（BLT）模型发现，在计算最优配置下模型参数量应与以字节（而非词元）衡量的数据量成正比地缩放，且最优压缩率不同于常用BPE分词器所得的结果。
en_tdlr: By training 988 latent tokenized (BLT) models with varying compression rates, this paper reveals that in compute-optimal configurations, model parameter counts scale proportionally to data size measured in bytes rather than tokens, and the optimal compression rate differs from that of a standard BPE tokenizer.
